newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end sharply higher, eye rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end sharply higher, eye rate cut.

text.p: Anticipation of a long-awaited interest rate cut drove South Korean shares to a sharply higher close for the fourth straight session on Wednesday.
Bolstered by across-the-board buying, the composite stock index rose 2.53 percent or 20.16 points to close provisionally at 817.78. Gainers led losers by 748 to 165 with 252 stocks going limit up.

"Lower interest rates are the major theme in the market," said Lee Yon-suk, broker at Citicorp International. "But I expect no further steep rises on the index. After some consolidation, the market will show steady rises."
"Investors believe the rate cut will help the financial status of companies and improve market liquidity," said analyst Hwang Chang-joong of LG Securities.

Economic planners and senior officials at the ruling New Korea Party agreed in principle that money market rates would soon be lowered by one to two percent to help domestic companies boost international competitiveness. A cut in the reserve requirement for banks is also being considered, officials said.
A party official said yields on three-year corporate bonds would fall to the 10 percent level. The corporate yield fell to 11.98 percent on Wednesday from 12.40 level early this week.
But the widely-expected ratio cut was not included in the government's economic package announced today in an economic ministers' meeting, designed to mend the ailing economy.
The package included slashing domestic steel prices and opening power production to private sector competition.
Brokers, however, said they were unimpressed. There was nothing in the package, they said, which could immediately revive the economy.
Buying remained strong in low-priced large-capitalised shares and construction issues which were seen as beneficiaries of any interest rate cut.
